To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cry1C delta endotoxin forms ionic channels in planar lipid membranes at high concentration, and that the size of the pores formed is similar to those observed with other Cry toxins.
Cry1C, like other Cry delta-endotoxics, forms channels with a radius of 1-1.3 nm in receptor-free bilayers.
the pores formed by Cry1c have a similar pore radius, and that the pore radius is between 1 and 1.5 nanometers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of pore formation by the Bacillus Thuringiensis (Bt) Cry1C delta endotoxin in planer lipid bilayers.
the mechanism by which the Bacillus thurengiensis Cry1Ac delta-endotoxin forms pores in lipid bilayer membranes.
the molecular basis of the mode of action and the mechanism of pore formation by the Bacillus Thuringiensis Cry delta-endotoxine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Cry1C toxin forms pores of a variable size, with the smallest pores of about 1 nm and the largest pores of about 3 nm in diameter, with the most frequent pore of about 1.5 nm in diameter, and with a pore radius of about 1 to 1.3 in diameter.
the Cry1C pore radius is between 1.05 and 1.35 nm.

the pores formed by Cry1Aa, Cry1Ab, Cry1Ac, Cry1C, Cry1D, Cry1E, Cry1Fa, Cry1Fb, Cry1Fg and Cry1Ia have similar pore sizes, which range between 1 and 1.5 nm, and that the pores formed in lipid bilayers by these toxins are large enough to accommodate the smallest known receptor-binding domains, which have a molecular mass of approximately 10 kDa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cry1C toxin is a pore forming protein.

the pores formed by Cry1A and Cry1C have similar radii, whereas the pores formed by these toxins differ in their conductance levels, suggesting that these two Cry1 toxins form pores having different structures.
Cry1C is the smallest delta-endotoxin that forms pores in planar lipid membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cry1C is a very good pore former and that the pore size of the Cry1C channels is larger than the pore size of any other insecticidal Cry toxin.
the Cry1C toxin forms a cluster composed of a variable numbers of channels having a pore radius of between ~1.0 and ~1.3 nm.
the pore formed by Cry1c is large enough to accommodate a single molecule of the Cry1Ac toxin.
